articles.title: BSP profit soars past ₱53 billion as forex gains offset revenue slump
articles.description: Surging foreign-exchange gains and sharp reductions in borrowing costs propelled the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) net income past ₱53 billion in the first two months of 2026, more than doubling its profit from a year earlier even as overall revenue contracted. Preliminary and unaudited financial statements from the central bank showed that net income after tax jumped 129 percent to ₱53.8 billion from ₱23.5 billion recorded in the January-to-February period of 2025. The primary driver behind the expansion was realized foreign-exchange gains, which rose to ₱45.2 billion from ₱22 billion in the previous year. The BSP generates these earnings from exchange-rate fluctuations during the execution and settlement of its foreign currency-denominated transactions. The bottom-line growth also cushioned a top-line slowdown. Total revenue dropped 13 percent to ₱33.5 billion at end-February from ₱38.5 billion during the same period last year. Interest income declined 16 percent to ₱31.5 billion from ₱37.5 billion, while miscellaneous income increased to ₱2 billion from ₱900 million. A substantial reduction in operational costs offset the revenue decline. Total expenditure fell 33 percent to ₱24.9 billion from ₱36.9 billion. The BSP benefited from lower interest expenses, which plummeted 39 percent to ₱14.2 billion from ₱23.2 billion, while other operational expenses contracted 22 percent to ₱10.7 billion. Consequently, net operational income before foreign-exchange gains reached ₱8.6 billion, expanding from the ₱1.5 billion generated in the prior-year period. The BSP’s total assets stood at ₱7.88 trillion at end-February, a 2.3 percent decrease from ₱8.07 trillion a year earlier. Gross international reserves, which reached ₱6.49 trillion, helped anchor the balance sheet against a decline in domestic securities holdings, which settled at ₱862.5 billion. Total liabilities shrank four percent to ₱7.52 trillion. Revaluation of foreign currency accounts expanded to ₱1.82 trillion from ₱1.21 trillion. Outstanding balances in the central bank's reverse repurchase facility narrowed to ₱200.6 billion from ₱239.4 billion, while domestic bills payable decreased to ₱339.4 billion from ₱898.3 billion. The central bank’s equity widened by 43 percent to ₱361.3 billion from ₱252.7 billion, lifted by an increase in surplus and reserves to ₱301.3 billion. Capital remained unchanged at ₱60 billion. The strong start to 2026 follows a profitable prior year. Audited figures show the monetary authority closed 2025 with a full-year net profit of ₱124.6 billion, up seven percent from ₱116.7 billion in 2024, supported by ₱265.6 billion in total revenues and ₱58.9 billion in net realized foreign-exchange gains.

articles.title: Ajit Agarkar set for crucial talks on his contract extension with BCCI officials; fate to be decided over next 48 hours: Report
articles.description: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and chief selector Ajit Agarkar are navigating a critical junction regarding his contract renewal, which officially expires on October 4, 2026. Despite recent rumors of friction, a report published by Sportstar claims that both sides are actively working toward sorting out their differences. According to the report, Agarkar will sit down with some BCCI officials over the next 48 hours to discuss a ‘roadmap’ for his extension. “Both parties were positively looking at extension and hoped that a few teething issues could be sorted out at the earliest,” the publication quoted a BCCI functionary as saying. Under BCCI regulations, a member can serve a maximum of four consecutive years on a senior selection committee. Having taken the helm in July 2023, Agarkar remains fully eligible for this remaining one-year term. Ajit Agarkar's position came under scrutiny after the July 2026 ODI series against England, where Rohit Sharma's future in ODI cricket and leaked retirement timelines left a section of BCCI officials furious. Rumours surfaced during the England tour that the selection committee had discussed dropping Rohit from future ODI assignments and that the Lord's match would be his last. After the veteran opener slammed a century in that game, the narrative backfired, prompting BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia to issue a public statement confirming Sharma's long-term spot in the team. For now, Agarkar continues to occupy the chairman of selectors post. However, the upcoming meeting with the BCCI top brass could determine whether he continues to hold the role or the board opts for a change. If he doesn’t get extension, the board will need a replacement just a year before the 2027 ODI World Cup in Africa. Agarkar’s tenure has brought immense white-ball success to the Indian team, including three ICC titles (2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups and 2025 Champions Trophy) and two Asia Cups. While limited-overs results have been historic, the team’s graph has gone down considerably in the Test format, suffering clean sweeps at the hands of New Zealand and South Africa in home series. The Agarkar-led panel has also managed a major transition phase, with Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli stepping away from Tests and T20Is, alongside red-ball exits for Ravichandran Ashwin, Cheteshwar Pujara, and Ajinkya Rahane.
